text:
Before applying the tools, you must understand what actually goes wrong in the brain during trauma, withdrawal or chronic stress, the "Hardware Failures" the tools are for.

If you've tried to talk yourself out of a trigger and couldn't, that's because anatomy overrides intellect. Dr. Perry describes a "Metabolic Red Line" for the traumatized brain: once your resting heart rate goes up or your heart-rate variability drops (a state of "Fear"), blood flow shifts away from the Cortex, which does logic and reasoning, and down to the Brainstem, which runs survival.

So if you try to process trauma while you're above this red line, you're adding to the armor instead of taking it off. In that state your functional IQ drops a lot, and the Nucleus Accumbens gets flooded with the catecholamines that transcribe new DeltaFosB proteins, the "armor" itself.
section: Part 1: THE SCIENCE (Why We Do This)
reader: someone deciding whether to use the protocol, who wants to know what is going wrong in their brain first

sentences.s: Before applying the tools, you must understand what actually goes wrong in the brain during trauma, withdrawal or chronic stress, the "Hardware Failures" the tools are for.

sentences.s: If you've tried to talk yourself out of a trigger and couldn't, that's because anatomy overrides intellect.

sentences.s: Dr. Perry describes a "Metabolic Red Line" for the traumatized brain: once your resting heart rate goes up or your heart-rate variability drops (a state of "Fear"), blood flow shifts away from the Cortex, which does logic and reasoning, and down to the Brainstem, which runs survival.
sentences.payoff: they learn the signs (heart rate up, HRV down) and what happens in the brain past them
sentences.follows: gives the mechanism behind that experience, with the red line the heading names

sentences.s: So if you try to process trauma while you're above this red line, you're adding to the armor instead of taking it off.
sentences.payoff: they learn when not to do trauma work: above the red line, it builds armor
sentences.follows: draws what the red line means for trauma work, the paragraph's point, first

sentences.s: In that state your functional IQ drops a lot, and the Nucleus Accumbens gets flooded with the catecholamines that transcribe new DeltaFosB proteins, the "armor" itself.
sentences.payoff: they learn why: thinking drops and the chemistry that builds the armor floods in

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
